title: AI-measured retinal vessel metrics nominally linked to cognitive impairment in diabetes
summary: In 630 community-dwelling adults with type 2 diabetes from four Guiyang health centres, the EVision AI system quantified retinal vascular density and fractal dimensions from fundus photographs. Mild cognitive impairment by MoCA-B affected 33.2% (n=209); after adjustment, vascular density (OR 0.987 per 1%), fractal dimension (OR 0.221 per 0.1, 95% CI 0.050-0.982) and vessel-centerline fractal dimension (OR 0.359 per 0.1) were nominally associated with lower odds, with consistent directions across age and diabetes-duration strata; sensitivity analyses supported only vascular density and centerline fractal dimension. The design is cross-sectional with MoCA-B screening rather than diagnosis, 132 participants were excluded (117 for image failure), and the associations are exploratory and not causal.
ai_technology: EVision AI system (deep learning and computer vision) quantifying retinal vascular density, fractal dimension and tortuosity from fundus photographs.
organization: Guizhou Center for Disease Control and Prevention; Affiliated Hospital of Guizhou Medical University

evidence.tested: Retrospective-style cross-sectional logistic regression with DAG-derived covariates plus stratified and sensitivity analyses.
evidence.unknown: Cross-sectional; MoCA-B screening, not clinical diagnosis; exploratory nominal associations with wide intervals; image-quality exclusions; no prospective or external validation.
evidence.ai_role: A pre-existing deep-learning retinal analysis platform derives the vascular metrics that are the study exposures; the AI was not newly developed here.

source_review.scope: PMC full text read independently (methods, AI quantification, results tables, exclusions, limitations); received 17 Mar, accepted 25 Sep, online 23 Nov 2026 (Crossref); no earlier version found in Europe PMC or Crossref; catalog duplicate check none.
